answer: To keep standing, each identity must win a scarce interrogation berth at the verification wharf and solve a challenge salted with its own prior-answer hashes. Newcomers reach that queue only through a single-file inlet: one unproven identity per established sponsor per day, each posting a deposit. Because salts differ per history, copied answers fail; an attacker running N Sybils must buy N berths and solve N distinct challenges in wall-clock time. Missed or colliding slots slash the deposit to its nadir, so mass forgery is both capital- and latency-expensive.
